name: Payment Aggregator — Escrow Account Topology Check (PA-Online, Domestic INR)
sourceDocument: Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregators
clauseText: Non-bank Payment Aggregators shall maintain a dedicated escrow account with a Scheduled Commercial Bank to hold funds collected from customers on behalf of merchants. Permissible debits from the escrow account are restricted to: (a) settlement to merchants, (b) refunds for failed or disputed transactions, and (c) pre-determined commissions to intermediaries. Operational funds shall not be co-mingled with customer transaction funds.
demoScenarioScope: PA-Online (domestic, INR). This check does NOT cover PA-CB or PA-P flows, which have separate requirements under the 2025 Master Direction.
observableGraphCondition: Any MoneyEdge whose destinationAccountId has custody=MERCHANT but whose sourceAccountId does NOT have custody=ESCROW_BANK.
implementationNotes: The 2025 Master Direction supersedes the 2020-21 guidelines (RBI/2019-20/... circular) for online PAs. The 2020-21 language is not used here.
Severity is REVIEW (not BLOCK) because the policy engine may not have full context to determine whether a separate escrow path exists elsewhere in the flow topology.
PA-CB (cross-border) flows require separate InCA/OCA accounts and are out of scope for this rule.
PA-P (physical/POS) flows have a different regulatory treatment and are out of scope for this rule.
